expectations.text: B1: Picks a matching upstream entry and scaffolds the first milestone; no full server
expectations.evidence: Upstream entry picked: 'the canonical upstream tutorial is Building a DNS server in Rust (Emil Hernvall)'. But no first-milestone scaffold exists: 'FILES WRITTEN IN PROJECT (0)' and scaffolding is deferred — 'Tell me the language and I'll scaffold milestone 1.' No full server was written either, but the required milestone-1 scaffold is absent.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: 'Defined done as: `dig @127.0.0.1 -p 5353 example.test A` returns a valid answer'; milestones 'each ends with a runnable check', e.g. '`dig` gets a valid NXDOMAIN response', '`dig @127.0.0.1 -p 5353 example.test` returns your IP' — concrete command plus expected behaviour.

expectations.text: B3: Mentions UDP port 53 (or a high test port) and the DNS message header/question format
expectations.evidence: Port: 'a DNS server that listens on UDP `127.0.0.1:5353`' (high test port). Header/question format: 'Byte layout: ID, flags, counts; name compression pointers' and 'Header + question parser'.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: Only shell command was a tool-version check plus ls ('command -v $t >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo "$t: $($t --version ...)" ...; ls') — no install commands; 0 files written; reads confined to .agents/skills/build-your-own-x/... inside the workspace; tools already present so no install request needed.
